==English==
{{wp}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪts/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɪʔ.s/|a=Pacific Northwest}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-its.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪts|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|it's}}

===Etymology 1===
Equivalent to {{affix|en|it|-s<id:possessive pronoun><pos:possessive marker>}}. From the earlier form {{m|en|it's}} ({{compound|en|it|-'s<id:possessive>}}), which is now considered nonstandard. Began to displace {{m|en|his}} as the possessive of the neuter pronoun in the Middle English period; had fully displaced it by the 1700s.<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref>

====Alternative forms====
* {{l|en|it's}} {{qualifier|now nonstandard}}

====Determiner====
{{head|en|determiner|cat2=possessive determiners}}

# Belonging to [[it]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=43|book=I|passage=The manner wherewith our Lawes assay to moderate the foolish and vaine expences of table-cheare and apparell, seemeth contrarie to '''it's''' end.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1751|translator=Thomas More|author=G. Burnett|title=Utopia
|passage=since I have been at the Pains to write it, if he consents to '''it's''' being published I will follow my Friend's Advice, and chiefly yours.}}
#*: That which groweth of '''its''' own accord of thy harvest thou shalt not reap, neither gather the grapes of thy vine undressed: for it is a year of rest unto the land. {{qualifier|originally "of it own accord" in the 1611 first edition}}
#* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|passage=They descended the hill, crossed the bridge, and drove to the door; and, while examining the nearer aspect of the house, all her apprehensions of meeting '''its''' owner returned.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Jasper Becker; John Gittings|journal=w:The Guardian|date=1989-06-05
|passage=The Chinese government is at war with '''its''' own people.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Lilit Marcus|title=Japan may be sick of mass tourism. But the deer in this ancient UNESCO-listed city love it|url=https://www.cnn.com/travel/japan-overtourism-nara-deer-intl-hnk|date=2024-07-23|passage=Nara and '''its''' deer are so closely associated that the light-brown colored animals are pictured in the city’s tourism ads, on buses, train tickets and more.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260416020347/https://www.cnn.com/travel/japan-overtourism-nara-deer-intl-hnk/|archivedate=16 April 2026}}

====Pronoun====
{{head|en|pronoun|cat2=possessive pronouns|cat3=third person pronouns}}

# The one (or ones) belonging to it. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=October 1 2007|author=Ian Austen|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/01/technology/01ebay.html|title=Canadian Court Opens Up eBay Data to Tax Agency
|passage=EBay Canada argued in court that the data sought by tax collectors was not '''its''' to give.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251107060354/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/01/technology/01ebay.html|archivedate=7 November 2025}}

====Usage notes====
* In practice, ''its'' is commonly used as a determiner before a noun, but its use as a solo pronoun is generally avoided.
* ''Its'' is now distinguished from {{m|en|it's}} (a [[contraction]] of "it is" or "it has"). For example, '''''It's''' going to rain'' is equivalent to '''''It is''' going to rain'', and '''''It's''' been raining for hours'' is equivalent to '''''It has''' been raining for hours.'' However, the two are commonly confused, and using ''its'' where there should be ''it's'' (or vice versa) is a common mistake in written English.
* Like ''it'', ''its'' is usually avoided when referring to humans. ''Its'' is commonly used with animals when the gender is unknown or unimportant. However, ''its'' could be used if the person who can't be seen clearly is described as a {{m|en|figure}}, {{m|en|shape}}, {{m|en|silhouette}}, etc. E.g. ''The '''figure''' moved behind a bush, but Josh could see '''its''' shadow from the moonlight.''

====See also====

[…]}}|series=The Physitian’s Library|location=London|publisher={{...|Printed by}} Peter Cole{{nb...|Printer and Book-seller, at the Sign of the Printing-press in Cornhil near the Royal Exchange.}}|page=31|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/2751056R.nlm.nih.gov/page/n40/mode/1up|oclc=14324814|passage=The Fleſh of man, becauſe '''its''' Nouriſhed by purer Blood, is delicater than the fleſh of other Creatures, and prefered before it by Canibals, or Man-Eaters.}}
